definition_en: a strong post in the ground, a share in a business, or something important that may be lost
core_image: 一根木桩被敲进松软的泥土
scene: 他把木桩敲进土里。He drove the stake into the ground.
sceneCN: 这里 stake 是「木桩」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他把木桩敲进土里。

senses.title: Pointed post
senses.definition: a strong pointed post driven into the ground
senses.definitionCN: 打进地里的结实尖桩
senses.example: He drove the stake into the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 他把木桩敲进土里。
senses.why: This is the oldest concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、最具体的义项。

senses.title: Share or interest
senses.definition: a share in a business or a personal interest in something
senses.definitionCN: 企业中的股份，或对某事的切身利益
senses.example: She has a stake in the company.
senses.exampleCN: 她在这家公司有股份。
senses.why: A marker in the ground became a claim on value.
senses.whyCN: 插在地上的标志，变成了对价值的份额。

senses.title: Risk something
senses.definition: to risk money or something valuable on a result
senses.definitionCN: 为某个结果拿钱财或珍贵之物冒险
senses.example: He staked his reputation on the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿自己的声誉押在这个计划上。
senses.why: The noun of a pledge became a verb of risking.
senses.whyCN: 作为抵押物的名词，转为冒险的动词。

intro.en: Stake comes from Old English staca, a post, from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: stake 来自古英语 staca（桩），源于日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root meant a post or peg.
Staca meant a pointed post.
Stake named a post marking a boundary.
A marked claim became a share of value.
items.cn: 标出的所有权变成价值份额。

items.en: The verb sense of risking grew.
items.cn: 「冒险押上」的动词义发展起来。

note.en: Stake is compared with look-alike words and words for posts or shares.
note.cn: 把 stake 与形近词以及表示桩或份额的词作比较。

entries.definition: a strong upright piece of wood
to risk money on a result
a part of a company's value

normalIntro.en: Stake is a post in the ground, a claim marked by it, and the risk behind the claim.
normalIntro.cn: stake 是插在地上的桩，是它标出的权利，也是权利背后的风险。

normal.en: Tie the tent to the stake.
He has a stake in the firm.
Our future is at stake.
They staked a claim to the land.
normal.cn: 他们对这块土地提出了所有权要求。

normal.en: She staked her savings on the race.
normal.cn: 她把积蓄押在了比赛上。

abstract.en: A post marks what a hand claims.
abstract.cn: 一根桩，标出一只手所认领的东西。

abstract.en: What you own is also what you may lose.
abstract.cn: 你拥有的，也是你可能失去的。

abstract.en: Every claim has a risk tied to it.
abstract.cn: 每一份权利，都系着风险。

examples.en: He drove the stake into the ground.
examples.cn: 他把木桩敲进土里。

examples.en: She has a stake in the company.
examples.cn: 她在这家公司有股份。

examples.en: He staked his reputation on the plan.
examples.cn: 他拿自己的声誉押在这个计划上。

dict_mnemonic.text: stake 是「木桩」，也指「股份、利害关系」，动词意为「押上」；at stake 是事关重大，have a stake in 是与……有利害关系。

root: 来自古英语 staca（桩），源于日耳曼语词根；由插桩标界引申为所有权与股份，再引申为拿有价值之物冒险。

sensesIntro.en: Stake means a post, a share or interest, or to risk something valuable.
sensesIntro.cn: stake 指木桩、股份与利害关系，或拿珍贵之物冒险。

core.en: A marker driven into the ground.

branches.en: A mallet drives wood into soil.
branches.cn: 木槌把木头打进泥土。

branches.en: A name sits on a list of owners.
branches.cn: 一个名字出现在股东名单上。

branches.en: Coins are pushed across a table.
branches.cn: 硬币被推过桌面。

branches.en: The post and the share both mark a claim.
branches.cn: 木桩与股份，都在标出权利。

branches.en: To hold a share is to carry a risk.
branches.cn: 持有股份，就承担风险。

intro.en: Stake forms verb parts and compounds of claim and watch.
intro.cn: stake 构成动词变化以及表示认领与监视的复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.exampleCN: 每位利益相关者都发了言。

items.example: They set a stake net in the river.
items.exampleCN: 他们在河里架起了桩网。

definition_zh: 不新鲜的；陈旧的；走味的
definition_en: no longer fresh, or no longer interesting because it is too familiar
core_image: 一块放久了变硬的面包
scene: 面包放久变硬了。The bread has gone stale.
sceneCN: 这里 stale 是「不新鲜的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：面包放久变硬了。

senses.title: Not fresh
senses.definition: no longer fresh, especially of food
senses.definitionCN: 尤指食物不再新鲜
senses.example: The bread has gone stale.
senses.exampleCN: 面包放久变硬了。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的物理义项。

senses.title: Old and dull
senses.definition: no longer interesting because it is too familiar
senses.definitionCN: 因过于熟悉而不再有趣
senses.example: His jokes are getting stale.
senses.exampleCN: 他的笑话越来越老套。
senses.why: Food going stale became ideas going dull.
senses.whyCN: 食物变味，引申为想法乏味。

senses.title: Without life
senses.definition: flat or lifeless, as of air or a performance
senses.definitionCN: 指空气或表演沉闷、缺乏生气
senses.example: The room was full of stale air.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里满是污浊的空气。
senses.why: Staleness can be felt without taste.
senses.whyCN: 「不新鲜」不靠尝也能感觉到。

intro.en: Stale comes from Old French estale, fixed or standing, of uncertain deeper origin.
intro.cn: stale 来自古法语 estale（固定不动的），更早来源不确定。

items.en: The deeper origin is not certain.
Estale meant fixed or settled.
items.cn: estale 意为固定的、停滞的。

items.en: Stale described drink or food gone flat.
items.cn: stale 描述走味的饮料或食物。

items.en: The sense widened to anything old.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何陈旧之物。

items.en: Stale jokes and stale air both became common.
items.cn: 「老掉牙的笑话」和「污浊的空气」都成了常见说法。

note.en: Stale is compared with look-alike words and words for old or dry.
note.cn: 把 stale 与形近词以及表示陈旧或干燥的词作比较。

entries.definition: having existed for a long time

normalIntro.en: Stale means time has taken the freshness out of food, air, or jokes.
normalIntro.cn: stale 指时间抽走了食物、空气或笑话里的新鲜感。

normal.en: This bread is stale.
Open a window; the air is stale.
The joke felt stale.
Their marriage had gone stale.
normal.cn: 他们的婚姻已失去活力。

normal.en: Stale smoke hung in the room.
normal.cn: 陈腐的烟味滞留在房间里。

abstract.en: Even honey loses its shine in time.
abstract.cn: 再甜的蜜，也会随时间失去光泽。

abstract.en: Repetition turns wonder into habit.
abstract.cn: 重复把惊奇变成习惯。

abstract.en: Freshness is a guest, not a resident.
abstract.cn: 新鲜是客人，不是常住户。

examples.en: The bread has gone stale.
examples.cn: 面包放久变硬了。

examples.en: His jokes are getting stale.
examples.cn: 他的笑话越来越老套。

examples.en: The room was full of stale air.
examples.cn: 房间里满是污浊的空气。

dict_mnemonic.text: stale 是「不新鲜的、陈旧的」；stale bread 是不新鲜的面包，stale air 是污浊的空气，go stale 是变味、变陈旧。

root: 来自古法语 estale（固定不动的），更早来源不确定；由「停滞不动」引申为食物走味、空气沉闷、想法陈旧。

sensesIntro.en: Stale means no longer fresh, old and dull, or flat and lifeless.
sensesIntro.cn: stale 指不再新鲜、陈旧乏味，或沉闷无生气。

core.en: Freshness lost through time.

branches.en: A loaf hardens on the shelf.
branches.cn: 面包在架子上变硬。

branches.en: A familiar joke draws no laugh.
branches.cn: 熟悉的笑话引不来笑声。

branches.en: Closed windows keep the room heavy.
branches.cn: 关着的窗让房间沉闷。

branches.en: Food and humour both lose their edge.
branches.cn: 食物与幽默，都会失去锋芒。

branches.en: What is repeated becomes airless.
branches.cn: 被重复的东西，会变得不透气。

intro.en: Stale forms comparisons, an adverb, and a noun.
intro.cn: stale 构成比较级、副词和名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word came through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，经古法语传入。

items.example: That is the stalest joke here.
items.exampleCN: 那是这里最老套的笑话。
那句话被陈腐地重复着。

items.example: The staleness of the air was clear.
They fed stale bread to the birds.
items.exampleCN: 他们把不新鲜的面包喂鸟。

definition_en: a small open shop, to stop working suddenly, or to delay
core_image: 市场里摆满水果的木制摊位
scene: 市场里的摊位摆满了水果。The stall in the market was full of fruit.
sceneCN: 这里 stall 是「摊位」（第 1 个义项）；句意：市场里的摊位摆满了水果。

senses.title: Market stand
senses.definition: a small open stand where goods are sold
senses.definitionCN: 出售商品的小型敞开货摊
senses.example: The stall in the market was full of fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 市场里的摊位摆满了水果。
senses.why: This is the familiar noun sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的名词义项。

senses.title: Engine stops
senses.definition: to stop working suddenly, as an engine
senses.definitionCN: 发动机等突然停止运转
senses.example: The car stalled at the lights.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车在红绿灯处熄火了。
senses.why: A standstill became a mechanical stop.
senses.whyCN: 「停住」变成了机械上的熄火。

senses.title: Delay
senses.definition: to delay something on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意推迟某事
senses.example: They stalled the talks for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把谈判拖了一周。
senses.why: Stopping progress became delaying it.
senses.whyCN: 让进程停住，就是拖延。

intro.en: Stall comes from Old English steall, a standing place, from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: stall 来自古英语 steall（站立之处），源于日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root meant a place to stand.
Steall meant a standing place or stable.
items.cn: steall 意为站立处或马厩。

items.en: Stall named a booth for selling.
items.cn: stall 指出售货物的棚摊。

items.en: The verb sense of stopping appeared.
Delaying became a common verb sense.

note.en: Stall is compared with look-alike words and words for stands or stops.
note.cn: 把 stall 与形近词以及表示摊位或停止的词作比较。

entries.definition: to be upright on the feet
a small closed or open stand

normalIntro.en: Stall is a place to stand and sell, and then any sudden stop.
normalIntro.cn: stall 原是一个站着卖东西的地方，后来也指任何突然的停顿。

normal.en: She runs a flower stall.
The engine stalled twice.
He stalled for time.
The market stalls open early.
Talks have stalled again.

abstract.en: A stand becomes a stop.
abstract.cn: 一个立着的地方，变成了停下的地方。

abstract.en: Delay is a stall in time.
abstract.cn: 拖延，是时间里的抛锚。

abstract.en: What cannot move forward must wait.
abstract.cn: 无法前进的，只能等待。

examples.en: The stall in the market was full of fruit.
examples.cn: 市场里的摊位摆满了水果。

examples.en: The car stalled at the lights.
examples.cn: 汽车在红绿灯处熄火了。

examples.en: They stalled the talks for a week.
examples.cn: 他们把谈判拖了一周。

dict_mnemonic.text: stall 是「摊位」，动词意为「熄火、拖延」；market stall 是市场摊位，stall for time 是拖延时间；过去式加 ed 变 stalled。

root: 来自古英语 steall（站立之处），源于日耳曼语词根；由摆摊的「立脚点」引申为发动机停转与人故意拖延。

sensesIntro.en: Stall means a market stand, an engine stopping, or a deliberate delay.
sensesIntro.cn: stall 指市场摊位、发动机熄火，或故意拖延。

core.en: A fixed place where movement pauses.
core.cn: 运动暂停下来的固定之处。

branches.en: Fruit is stacked on a wooden table.
branches.cn: 水果堆在木桌上。

branches.en: A engine coughs and goes silent.
branches.cn: 发动机咳了两声便安静了。

branches.en: Papers are shuffled to fill time.
branches.cn: 人们翻动文件来耗时间。

branches.en: A stand and a stop share one word.
branches.cn: 摊位与停顿，共用一个词。

branches.en: Machine and lawyer can both stall.
branches.cn: 机器与律师，都能「停住」。

intro.en: Stall forms verb parts and a few market words.
intro.cn: stall 构成动词变化和若干与摊位相关的词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.meaning: a person who runs a stall

definition_en: a small piece of paper for postage, a tool that prints a mark, or to bring the foot down hard
core_image: 一枚邮票被贴在信封右上角
scene: 他在信封上贴了一张邮票。He put a stamp on the envelope.
sceneCN: 这里 stamp 是「邮票」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他在信封上贴了一张邮票。

senses.title: Postage label
senses.definition: a small piece of paper stuck on mail to show payment
senses.definitionCN: 贴在邮件上表示已付邮资的小纸片
senses.example: He put a stamp on the envelope.
senses.exampleCN: 他在信封上贴了一张邮票。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最日常的义项。

senses.title: Printed mark or tool
senses.definition: a tool that prints a design, or the mark it makes
senses.definitionCN: 印出图案的工具，或它留下的印记
senses.example: The letter bears an official stamp.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信上盖着官方印章。
senses.why: The tool and its mark share one name.
senses.whyCN: 工具与印记共用一个词。

senses.title: Bring the foot down
senses.definition: to bring your foot down hard on the ground
senses.definitionCN: 用力把脚踩向地面
senses.example: She stamped her foot in anger.
senses.exampleCN: 她气得直跺脚。
senses.why: The old pounding action survived as a verb.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「捣击」动作保留在动词里。

intro.en: Stamp comes from Middle English stampen, to pound, from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: stamp 来自中古英语 stampen（捣、踏），源于日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root meant to pound or crush.
Stampen meant to bring the foot down.
A stamp named a tool that presses a mark.
items.cn: stamp 指压印图案的工具。

items.en: The postage stamp borrowed the name.
The verb kept the sense of heavy stepping.
items.cn: 动词保留了重重踩踏的含义。

note.en: Stamp is compared with look-alike words and words for marks.
note.cn: 把 stamp 与形近词以及表示印记的词作比较。

entries.definition: to be upright on the feet
to look at something for a long time
a mark or object that closes a document

normalIntro.en: Stamp began as a heavy step and now marks mail, paper, and anger.
normalIntro.cn: stamp 原是重重一踏，如今标记邮件、文件，也表达怒气。

normal.en: Stick the stamp here.
The passport has a stamp.
He stamped the date on the form.
She stamped her foot.
He collects old stamps.

abstract.en: A stamp makes one mark for many papers.
abstract.cn: 一枚印章，为许多文件留下同一个记号。

abstract.en: Paper can carry a promise across the sea.
abstract.cn: 一张纸，能把承诺带过海洋。

abstract.en: Anger often leaves a mark on the ground.
abstract.cn: 怒气常常在地上留下印记。

examples.en: He put a stamp on the envelope.
examples.cn: 他在信封上贴了一张邮票。

examples.en: The letter bears an official stamp.
examples.cn: 这封信上盖着官方印章。

examples.en: She stamped her foot in anger.
examples.cn: 她气得直跺脚。

dict_mnemonic.text: stamp 是「邮票」，也指「印章、印记」，动词意为「跺脚、盖章」；postage stamp 是邮票，rubber stamp 是橡皮图章；过去式加 ed。

root: 来自中古英语 stampen（捣、踏），源于日耳曼语「重压」的词根；由跺脚、捣压引申为压印工具与印记，再指邮票。

sensesIntro.en: Stamp means a postage label, a printed mark or tool, or to tread hard.
sensesIntro.cn: stamp 指邮票、印章与印记，或用力跺脚。

core.en: A hard downward press that leaves a mark.

branches.en: A small paper square sticks to an envelope.
branches.cn: 一小方纸贴在信封上。

branches.en: Ink transfers a design onto a page.
branches.cn: 油墨把图案压到纸面。

branches.en: A heel strikes the floor.
branches.cn: 脚跟重重砸向地面。

branches.en: Mail and documents both carry a mark.
branches.cn: 邮件与文件，都带着印记。

branches.en: The tool and the foot share one force.
branches.cn: 印章与脚，用的是同一股力。

intro.en: Stamp forms verb parts, agent nouns, and mail compounds.
intro.cn: stamp 构成动词变化、施动名词和邮政复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: Stamping the paper takes a moment.
items.exampleCN: 给文件盖章只需一会儿。

items.meaning: a person or tool that stamps

items.example: Two stampers worked at the desk.
items.exampleCN: 两个盖章人在桌边工作。

definition_en: to be upright on your feet, to accept something difficult, or to be in a place
core_image: 一个人静静站在窗边向外望
scene: 她站在窗边。She stood by the window.
sceneCN: 这里 stand 是「站立」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她站在窗边。

senses.title: Be upright
senses.definition: to be upright on your feet
senses.definitionCN: 双脚直立站着
senses.example: She stood by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 她站在窗边。
senses.why: This is the basic posture sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的姿态义项。

senses.title: Tolerate
senses.definition: to accept something difficult without giving up
senses.definitionCN: 不放弃地承受困难之事
senses.example: I cannot stand the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 我受不了这噪音。
senses.why: Standing firm in body became bearing in mind.
senses.whyCN: 身体站稳，引申为心理承受。

senses.title: Be located
senses.definition: to be placed or located in a position
senses.definitionCN: 处于某个位置
senses.example: The house stands on a hill.
senses.exampleCN: 房子坐落在小山上。
senses.why: A standing object marks its place.
senses.whyCN: 立着的东西标出自己的位置。

intro.en: Stand comes from Old English standan, to stand, from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: stand 来自古英语 standan（站立），源于日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root meant to stand still.
Standan meant to be upright.
Stand kept the posture sense.
The sense of bearing something grew.
The sense of being located became common.

note.en: Stand is compared with look-alike words and words for bearing or placing.
note.cn: 把 stand 与形近词以及表示承受或位置的词作比较。

entries.definition: to look at something for a long time
to get up from a seat

normalIntro.en: Stand is the body upright, the mind bearing, and a building holding its place.
normalIntro.cn: stand 是身体直立、心里承受，也是建筑守住位置。

normal.en: Please stand up.
They stood in line.
I can't stand the heat.
The old tower still stands.
The shop stands near the bridge.

abstract.en: To stand is to hold your ground.
abstract.cn: 站立，就是守住自己的位置。

abstract.en: What stands can also withstand.
abstract.cn: 能站住的，也能承受。

abstract.en: A place is known by what stands there.
abstract.cn: 一个地方，因立在那里的事物而被记住。

examples.en: She stood by the window.
examples.cn: 她站在窗边。

examples.en: I cannot stand the noise.
examples.cn: 我受不了这噪音。

examples.en: The house stands on a hill.
examples.cn: 房子坐落在小山上。

dict_mnemonic.text: stand 是「站立、忍受、位于」；stand up 是起立，stand for 是代表，can't stand 是无法忍受；过去式与过去分词都是 stood。

core.en: Being upright and holding a place.

branches.en: Two feet press the floor.

branches.en: A tower holds its place for centuries.

branches.en: The body stands, the mind withstands.

definition_en: a rule or measure used to judge quality, a level of quality, or the usual accepted type
core_image: 一把用来衡量长度的尺子
scene: 这家旅馆达到很高的标准。The hotel meets a high standard.
sceneCN: 这里 standard 是「标准」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这家旅馆达到很高的标准。

senses.title: Rule for judging
senses.definition: a rule or measure used to judge quality or correctness
senses.definitionCN: 用来评判质量或正确性的规则或尺度
senses.example: The hotel meets a high standard.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆达到很高的标准。
senses.why: A rule for judging quality is the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 衡量质量的规则，是这个词的核心义项。

senses.title: Level reached
senses.definition: the level of quality that someone or something reaches
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物所达到的质量水平
senses.example: Her work is above the average standard.
senses.exampleCN: 她的工作高于一般水准。
senses.why: The measured level grew from the rule itself.
senses.whyCN: 被衡量的水准，由规则本身引申而来。

senses.title: Usual type
senses.definition: of the usual or accepted type, not special
senses.definitionCN: 属于通常或公认类型的，非特殊的
senses.example: This is the standard model.
senses.exampleCN: 这是标准型号。
senses.why: Anything of the accepted type is called standard.
senses.whyCN: 凡属公认类型的事物，都称作标准的。

items.en: It named an accepted rule for judging quality.

normalIntro.en: Standard is a rule that measures quality, the level reached, and the usual type.

normal.en: Her work is above the average standard.

abstract.en: A level reached becomes a level expected.

abstract.en: What most people accept becomes standard.

intro.en: Standard forms verbs and nouns of measuring, and compounds of standing.

definition_en: a position from which someone views or judges an issue
core_image: 一个人站在原地观察四周
scene: 从她的立场看，这个决定合理。From her standpoint, the decision makes sense.
sceneCN: 这里 standpoint 是「立场」（第 1 个义项）；句意：从她的立场看，这个决定合理。

senses.title: Side taken
senses.definition: the side that a person stands on in a discussion or dispute
senses.definitionCN: 在讨论或争论中一个人所站的一方
senses.example: From her standpoint, the decision makes sense.
senses.exampleCN: 从她的立场看，这个决定合理。
senses.why: The physical place of standing is the base image.
senses.whyCN: 站立的具体位置，是这个词的基础意象。

senses.title: Opinion held
senses.definition: a particular opinion about an issue
senses.definitionCN: 对某个问题的特定看法
senses.example: The report reflects the standpoint of young workers.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告反映了年轻工人的观点。
senses.why: A place to stand became a side to take.
senses.whyCN: 站立之处，引申为所持的立场。

senses.title: Angle of view
senses.definition: the angle from which something is viewed or told
senses.definitionCN: 观察或叙述事物的角度
senses.example: The story is told from a child's standpoint.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事从孩子的视角讲述。
senses.why: A position in space became an angle of view.
senses.whyCN: 空间中的位置，引申为观察的视角。

intro.en: Standpoint joins the English verb stand with point, a word from Latin.
intro.cn: standpoint 由英语动词 stand 与源自拉丁语的 point 组合而成。

items.en: Stand meant to be upright on the feet.
Punctum meant a small mark or point.
Point entered English through Old French.
items.cn: point 经古法语进入英语。

items.cn: 两个词先组合出「站立之处」的意思。

items.en: It came to mean a mental position.

note.en: Standpoint is compared with look-alike words and words for points of view.

senses.title: Light in the sky

senses.exampleCN: 会议九点开始。
senses.why: Beginning an action is the central sense.
senses.whyCN: 开始一个动作，是这个词的中心义项。

senses.title: Set out
senses.definition: to leave a place and begin a journey
senses.definitionCN: 离开某地并开始一段旅程
senses.example: We started for the airport at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 我们黎明时出发去机场。
senses.why: Setting out is beginning a journey.
senses.whyCN: 出发，就是开始一段旅程。

senses.title: Make it run
senses.definition: to make a machine or engine begin working
senses.definitionCN: 使机器或发动机开始运转
senses.example: The car won't start in cold weather.
senses.exampleCN: 天冷时这辆车启动不了。
senses.why: Making a machine run is beginning its motion.
senses.whyCN: 让机器运转，就是开始它的运动。

intro.en: Start comes from Old English styrtan, to leap up, from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: start 来自古英语 styrtan（跳起），源于日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root described a sudden jump.
items.cn: 该词根描述突然的一跳。

items.en: Styrtan meant to leap up.
Start meant to move suddenly.
It came to mean beginning a journey or action.
items.cn: 它转而表示开始旅程或行动。

items.en: A machine sense of beginning to run grew.
items.cn: 「机器开始运转」的义项发展起来。

note.en: Start is compared with look-alike words and words for beginning.
note.cn: 把 start 与形近词以及表示开始的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Start is to begin, to set out, or to make something run.
normalIntro.cn: start 是开始、出发，或让某物运转起来。

normal.en: The meeting starts at nine.
We started for the airport at dawn.
normal.cn: 我们黎明时出发去机场。

normal.en: The car won't start in cold weather.
normal.cn: 天冷时这辆车启动不了。

normal.en: She started a small business.
A good start makes the rest easier.
normal.cn: 良好的开端让后面更容易。

abstract.en: Every road begins at the first step.
abstract.cn: 每条路都从第一步开始。

abstract.en: To start is to choose one direction.
abstract.cn: 开始，就是选定一个方向。

abstract.en: The engine turns, and the journey exists.
abstract.cn: 引擎一转，旅程才存在。

examples.en: The meeting starts at nine.
examples.cn: 会议九点开始。

examples.en: We started for the airport at dawn.
examples.cn: 我们黎明时出发去机场。

examples.en: The car won't start in cold weather.
examples.cn: 天冷时这辆车启动不了。

dict_mnemonic.text: start 是「开始」，也是「出发」和「启动」；from the start 是从一开始，start up 是启动或开办，starter 是启动器。

root: 来自古英语 styrtan（跳起），源于日耳曼语词根；由猛然一跳，引申为动身出发、开始行动，再到机器开始运转。

sensesIntro.en: Start means to begin something, to set out, or to make an engine run.
sensesIntro.cn: start 指开始某事、动身出发，或启动发动机。

core.en: A sudden move that sets things going.
core.cn: 发起动作的那一下猛然移动。

branches.en: A runner waits for the gun.
branches.cn: 选手等待发令枪。

branches.en: A traveller leaves at dawn.
branches.cn: 旅人黎明时动身。

branches.en: A key turns in the ignition.
branches.cn: 钥匙在点火处转动。

branches.en: The race and the journey both begin with a first move.
branches.cn: 比赛与旅程，都从第一步开始。

branches.en: An action and an engine both need a trigger.
branches.cn: 行动与引擎，都需要一个触发。

intro.en: Start forms verb parts and nouns of beginning and setting out.
intro.cn: start 构成动词变化，以及表示开始与出发的名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.meaning: a thing that starts, or a first course
a new company or the act of starting
items.exampleCN: 这家初创公司发展很快。

definition_en: to suffer or die from lack of food, or to need something very much
core_image: 空空的碗和干裂的土地
scene: 庄稼歉收，村里人挨饿。Crops failed and the villagers starved.
sceneCN: 这里 starve 是「挨饿」（第 2 个义项）；句意：庄稼歉收，村里人挨饿。

senses.title: Die of hunger
senses.definition: to die from lack of food
senses.definitionCN: 因缺少食物而死亡
senses.example: Many animals starved that winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那个冬天许多动物饿死了。
senses.why: The oldest sense is death from hunger.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是因饥饿而死。

senses.title: Suffer hunger
senses.definition: to suffer greatly from lack of food
senses.definitionCN: 因缺少食物而饱受折磨
senses.example: Crops failed and the villagers starved.
senses.exampleCN: 庄稼歉收，村里人挨饿。
senses.why: The milder everyday sense is going hungry.
senses.whyCN: 较弱、更日常的义项是忍受饥饿。

senses.title: Need greatly
senses.definition: to need something very much
senses.definitionCN: 非常需要某物
senses.example: The plant is starving for light.
senses.exampleCN: 这株植物极需光照。
senses.why: Hunger became a metaphor for any great need.
senses.whyCN: 饥饿成为任何强烈需要的比喻。

intro.en: Starve comes from Old English steorfan, to die, from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: starve 来自古英语 steorfan（死），源于日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root meant to die or become stiff.
items.cn: 该词根意为死亡或变得僵硬。

items.en: Steorfan meant to die.
The word narrowed toward dying of hunger.
items.cn: 这个词逐渐缩小为因饥饿而死。

items.en: It also came to mean suffering hunger.
items.cn: 它也转而表示忍受饥饿。

items.en: A figurative sense of great need appeared.
items.cn: 表示强烈需要的比喻义出现。

note.en: Starve is compared with look-alike words and words for hunger or strong need.
note.cn: 把 starve 与形近词以及表示饥饿或强烈需要的词作比较。

entries.definition: to suffer from lack of food

normalIntro.en: Starve is to die of hunger, to suffer hunger, or to need something badly.
normalIntro.cn: starve 是因饥饿而死、忍受饥饿，或强烈需要某物。

normal.en: Many animals starved that winter.
normal.cn: 那个冬天许多动物饿死了。

normal.en: Crops failed and the villagers starved.
The plant is starving for light.
No child should starve to death.
He was starved of sleep.

abstract.en: An empty bowl teaches what full means.
abstract.cn: 空碗让人懂得什么是饱。

abstract.en: Hunger of the body can become hunger of the mind.
abstract.cn: 身体的饥饿，可以变成心灵的渴求。

abstract.en: To lack deeply is also to want deeply.
abstract.cn: 深深的匮乏，也是深深的渴望。

examples.en: Many animals starved that winter.
examples.cn: 那个冬天许多动物饿死了。

examples.en: Crops failed and the villagers starved.
examples.cn: 庄稼歉收，村里人挨饿。

examples.en: The plant is starving for light.
examples.cn: 这株植物极需光照。

dict_mnemonic.text: starve 是「饿死」，也指「挨饿」和「极需」；starve to death 是饿死，be starved of 是极度缺乏，starvation 是饥饿。

root: 来自古英语 steorfan（死），源于日耳曼语词根；原指死亡，后缩小为因饥饿而死，又引申为忍受饥饿与强烈渴求。

sensesIntro.en: Starve means to die of hunger, to suffer hunger, or to need something very much.
sensesIntro.cn: starve 指饿死、挨饿，或非常需要某物。

core.en: A body emptied of food.

branches.en: A dry field holds no grain.
branches.cn: 干旱的田里没有粮食。

branches.en: A family waits for a meal.
branches.cn: 一家人等待一顿饭。

branches.en: A plant leans toward the window.
branches.cn: 一株植物朝窗倾斜。

branches.en: Dying and suffering are two degrees of the same hunger.
branches.cn: 饿死与挨饿，是同一种饥饿的两个程度。

branches.en: The hungry body and the needy mind both long for more.
branches.cn: 饥饿的身体与渴求的心，都在盼望更多。

intro.en: Starve forms verb parts and nouns of hunger.
intro.cn: starve 构成动词变化，以及表示饥饿的名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.exampleCN: 没有帮助他们可能饿死。
饥饿是一种无声的危险。
一只饿瘦的猫在外面叫。

items.meaning: to force out by cutting food
items.example: They tried to starve out the town.
items.exampleCN: 他们企图断粮逼小镇投降。
半饥饿的工人们休息着。

definition_en: a country or its government, a region within a country, a condition, or to say something formally
core_image: 地图上一个有边界的国家
scene: 这个国家重视教育。The state invests in education.
sceneCN: 这里 state 是「国家」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这个国家重视教育。

senses.title: Country and government
senses.definition: a country together with its government
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家及其政府
senses.example: The state invests in education.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家重视教育。
senses.why: A political country is the oldest public sense.
senses.whyCN: 政治意义上的国家，是最古老的公共义项。

senses.title: Region of a country
senses.definition: a region within a country that has its own government
senses.definitionCN: 一国内拥有自己政府的地区
senses.example: Texas is a large state.
senses.exampleCN: 得克萨斯是一个大州。
senses.why: A federal country divides itself into states.
senses.whyCN: 联邦制国家把自己划分为州。

senses.title: Condition
senses.definition: the condition that someone or something is in
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物所处的状况
senses.example: The patient is in a stable state.
senses.exampleCN: 病人处于稳定状态。
senses.why: A standing condition is the Latin core of the word.
senses.whyCN: 「站立着的状况」，是这个词的拉丁语核心。

senses.title: Say formally
senses.definition: to say or write something in a clear, formal way
senses.definitionCN: 以清晰正式的方式说出或写出某事
senses.example: Please state your name.
senses.exampleCN: 请说出你的姓名。
senses.why: The noun of a condition became a verb of setting out.
senses.whyCN: 表示状况的名词，转为把事情摆出来的动词。

intro.en: State comes from Latin status, a standing or condition, through Old French estat.
intro.cn: state 经古法语 estat 来自拉丁语 status（站立；状况）。

items.en: Status meant a standing or condition.
Estat named a rank or a condition.
State meant a condition and an estate.
It named a political country.
items.cn: 它开始指政治意义上的国家。

items.en: The verb sense of stating facts grew.
items.cn: 「陈述事实」的动词义发展起来。

note.en: State is compared with look-alike words and words for countries or conditions.
note.cn: 把 state 与形近词以及表示国家或状况的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: State is a country, a region of one, a condition, or the act of saying something formally.
normalIntro.cn: state 是国家、国家的一个州、一种状况，或正式陈述的动作。

normal.en: The state invests in education.
Texas is a large state.
The patient is in a stable state.
Please state your name.
The house was in a poor state.

abstract.en: To stand is to hold a place among others.
abstract.cn: 站立，就是在众人中占据一个位置。

abstract.en: A country is a people standing together.
abstract.cn: 国家，是站在一起的人民。

abstract.en: To state a fact is to stand it before others.
abstract.cn: 陈述事实，就是把它摆到众人面前。

examples.en: The state invests in education.
examples.cn: 这个国家重视教育。

examples.en: The patient is in a stable state.
examples.cn: 病人处于稳定状态。

examples.en: Please state your name.
examples.cn: 请说出你的姓名。

dict_mnemonic.text: state 是「国家」，也是「州」「状态」，动词是「陈述」；state of mind 是心境，in a state of 是处于……状态。

root: 来自拉丁语 status（站立；状况），经古法语 estat 进入英语；由站立的姿态，引申为国家、状态与正式陈述。

sensesIntro.en: State means a country, a region of a country, a condition, or to say something formally.
sensesIntro.cn: state 指国家、国家的州、状况，或正式陈述某事。

core.en: A standing position among things.

branches.en: A flag flies over a parliament.
branches.cn: 一面旗在议会上方飘扬。

branches.en: A line divides one region from another.
branches.cn: 一条界线分开两个地区。

branches.en: A doctor reads a chart.
branches.cn: 医生查看图表。

branches.en: A speaker gives a clear account.
branches.cn: 发言者作出清楚的说明。

branches.en: A country and a condition are both a way of standing.
branches.cn: 国家与状况，都是一种站立的方式。

intro.en: State forms verb parts, nouns of saying, and adjectives of rank.
intro.cn: state 构成动词变化、表示陈述的名词，以及表示等级的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root status also gives static, station, and statue.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 status 还衍生出 static、station 和 statue。

items.example: The state built a new school.

items.exampleCN: 她正在陈述自己的看法。
他们走进一座宏伟的大厅。
这个无国籍家庭等待着。

items.meaning: the condition of being a state

definition_en: something said or written formally, or a record of money paid and received
core_image: 一份盖着公章的文件
scene: 公司发表了一份简短声明。The company issued a short statement.
sceneCN: 这里 statement 是「声明」（第 1 个义项）；句意：公司发表了一份简短声明。

senses.title: Formal announcement
senses.definition: an official or public announcement
senses.definitionCN: 官方或公开的宣布
senses.example: The company issued a short statement.
senses.exampleCN: 公司发表了一份简短声明。
senses.why: A public announcement is the most common sense.
senses.whyCN: 公开声明，是这个字最常见的义项。

senses.title: Clear account
senses.definition: a clear account of facts or views
senses.definitionCN: 对事实或看法的清楚说明
senses.example: Her statement of the facts was clear.
senses.exampleCN: 她对事实的陈述很清楚。
senses.why: Saying something plainly is the base sense.
senses.whyCN: 把事情平实地讲出来，是这个词的基础义。

senses.title: Financial record
senses.definition: a record showing money paid in and out
senses.definitionCN: 记录收支款项的单据
senses.example: He checked his bank statement.
senses.exampleCN: 他核对了银行对账单。
senses.why: A written account of money grew from the same idea.
senses.whyCN: 关于钱财的书面记录，也由同一思路引申而来。

intro.en: Statement is state plus the noun suffix -ment.
intro.cn: statement 由 state 加名词后缀 -ment 构成。

items.en: Status meant a standing or condition.
Estat named a condition or rank.
State could mean an account or an estate.
items.cn: state 可指叙述，也可指产业。

items.en: The suffix -ment formed statement, a thing stated.
items.cn: 后缀 -ment 构成 statement，即被陈述之物。

items.en: It also named a record of money.

note.en: Statement is compared with look-alike words and words for announcements.
note.cn: 把 statement 与形近词以及表示公告的词作比较。

entries.definition: a report or a record of money

normalIntro.en: A statement is something stated: a public announcement, a clear account, or a money record.

normal.en: The company issued a short statement.
normal.cn: 公司发表了一份简短声明。

normal.en: Her statement of the facts was clear.

normal.en: He checked his bank statement.

normal.cn: 警方录了一份书面陈述。

normal.en: The two statements do not agree.

abstract.en: To state is to place a fact where others can see it.
abstract.cn: 陈述，就是把事实放到众人看得见的地方。

abstract.en: A public statement gives a private thought a shape.
abstract.cn: 公开声明，让私下的想法有了形状。

abstract.en: A record of money is also a statement about trust.
abstract.cn: 钱财的记录，也是关于信任的陈述。

examples.en: The company issued a short statement.
examples.cn: 公司发表了一份简短声明。

examples.en: Her statement of the facts was clear.
examples.cn: 她对事实的陈述很清楚。

examples.en: He checked his bank statement.
examples.cn: 他核对了银行对账单。

sensesIntro.en: Statement means a formal announcement, a clear account, or a financial record.
sensesIntro.cn: statement 指正式声明、清楚的陈述，或财务报表。

core.en: Something put into words for others.
core.cn: 被形诸言语、给他人看的内容。

branches.en: A spokesperson faces the press.
branches.cn: 发言人面对记者。

branches.en: A witness tells what happened.
branches.cn: 证人讲述发生了什么。

branches.en: Numbers fill a monthly page.
branches.cn: 数字填满每月一页的账单。

branches.en: An announcement is a public account of facts.
branches.cn: 公告就是对事实的公开陈述。

branches.en: Both words and figures can state a truth.
branches.cn: 文字与数字，都能陈述事实。

intro.en: Statement is built from state and the noun suffix -ment.
intro.cn: statement 由 state 与名词后缀 -ment 构成。

latinIntro.en: The base state comes from Latin status.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 state 来自拉丁语 status。

definition_en: electricity that gathers on a surface, staying still rather than flowing as a current, or noise caused by it
core_image: 毛衣上噼啪作响的小火花
scene: 干燥的空气容易产生静电。Dry air easily produces static.
sceneCN: 这里 static 是「静电」（第 1 个义项）；句意：干燥的空气容易产生静电。

senses.title: Charge at rest
senses.definition: electric charge that gathers on a surface and does not flow
senses.definitionCN: 聚集在表面、不流动的电荷
senses.example: Dry air easily produces static.
senses.exampleCN: 干燥的空气容易产生静电。
senses.why: The concrete electrical sense is the base.
senses.whyCN: 具体的电学含义，是这个字的基础。

senses.title: Not moving
senses.definition: not moving or changing
senses.definitionCN: 不移动或不变化的
senses.example: The image on the screen is static.
senses.exampleCN: 屏幕上的图像是静态的。
senses.why: The Greek root meant causing to stand.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根意为使站立不动。

senses.title: Radio noise
senses.definition: noise in radio or sound caused by static electricity
senses.definitionCN: 由静电引起的收音机或声音噪声
senses.example: The radio was full of static.
senses.exampleCN: 收音机里满是静电干扰的噪声。
senses.why: The charge sense gave a name to the noise.
senses.whyCN: 电荷义又给这种噪声起了名字。

intro.en: Static comes from Greek statikos, causing to stand, through Latin staticus.
intro.cn: static 经拉丁语 staticus 来自希腊语 statikos（使站立）。

items.en: Statikos meant causing to stand.
Staticus kept the sense of standing still.
items.cn: staticus 保留了静止不动的含义。

items.en: Static described forces at rest.
It named electric charge that does not flow.
The sense of radio noise appeared.
items.cn: 收音机噪声的义项出现。

note.en: Static is compared with look-alike words and words for stillness.
note.cn: 把 static 与形近词以及表示静止的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Static is charge that stays still, anything not moving, and the noise that charge makes.
normalIntro.cn: static 是停住不动的电荷、静止不动的事物，以及电荷造成的噪声。

normal.en: Dry air easily produces static.
normal.cn: 干燥的空气容易产生静电。

normal.en: The image on the screen is static.
normal.cn: 屏幕上的图像是静态的。

normal.en: The radio was full of static.
normal.cn: 收音机里满是静电干扰的噪声。

normal.en: Prices have remained static for a year.
Static charge built up on the cloth.

abstract.en: What stands still stores its energy in place.
abstract.cn: 静止不动的东西，把能量储在原处。

abstract.en: A still image lets the eye rest.
abstract.cn: 静止的图像，让目光得以停留。

abstract.en: Noise is energy with nowhere to go.
abstract.cn: 噪声，是无处可去的能量。

examples.en: Dry air easily produces static.

branches.cn: 事物的状况与社会等级，都是站立的方式。

intro.en: Status is a Latin noun that forms plurals and common compounds.
intro.cn: status 是拉丁语名词，能构成复数与常见复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin status comes from stare, to stand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 status 来自 stare（站立）。

items.example: The car is a status symbol.

items.exampleCN: 追求地位的行为很常见。
她接了一份地位很高的工作。
低地位的工作常被忽视。

latinEntries.example: Stare is the source of status.
latinEntries.exampleCN: stare 是 status 的源头。

definition_en: to remain in a place, to continue in a state, or to live somewhere for a short time
core_image: 行李箱放在旅馆房间里
scene: 他们决定再住一晚。They decided to stay one more night.
sceneCN: 这里 stay 是「暂住」（第 3 个义项）；句意：他们决定再住一晚。

senses.title: Remain in place
senses.definition: to remain in a place instead of leaving
senses.definitionCN: 留在某处而不离开
senses.example: Please stay in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 请留在房间里。
senses.why: Remaining in a place is the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 留在某处，是这个词的核心义项。

senses.title: Continue to be
senses.definition: to continue in a particular state
senses.definitionCN: 继续处于某种状态
senses.example: Stay calm during the test.
senses.exampleCN: 考试时保持冷静。
senses.why: Remaining in place became remaining in a state.
senses.whyCN: 留在原处，引申为停留在某种状态。

senses.title: Live briefly
senses.definition: to live somewhere as a guest for a short time
senses.definitionCN: 作为客人短期住在某地
senses.example: They decided to stay one more night.
senses.exampleCN: 他们决定再住一晚。
senses.why: A short stay is a brief remaining.
senses.whyCN: 暂住，就是短暂地留下。

intro.en: Stay comes from Old French ester, to remain, from Latin stare, to stand.
intro.cn: stay 来自古法语 ester（停留），源于拉丁语 stare（站立）。

items.en: Stare meant to stand.
Ester meant to remain or stay.
Staye meant to remain in a place.
It came to mean continuing in a state.
items.cn: 它转而表示保持某种状态。

items.en: It named a short visit as a guest.
items.cn: 它也指作为客人的短期逗留。

note.en: Stay is compared with look-alike words and words for remaining.
note.cn: 把 stay 与形近词以及表示留下的词作比较。

entries.definition: to stay in a place or state

normalIntro.en: Stay is to remain in a place, to keep a state, or to be a guest for a while.
normalIntro.cn: stay 是留在某处、保持某种状态，或作为客人住上一阵。

normal.en: Please stay in the room.
Stay calm during the test.
They decided to stay one more night.
We stayed at home all day.
Let us stay in touch.

abstract.en: To stay is to refuse the pull of elsewhere.
abstract.cn: 留下，就是拒绝别处的牵引。

abstract.en: A calm mind stays when the world moves.
abstract.cn: 世界移动时，平静的心仍然留在原处。

abstract.en: A short stay can still feel like home.
abstract.cn: 短暂的逗留，也能像家一样。

examples.en: Please stay in the room.
examples.cn: 请留在房间里。

examples.en: Stay calm during the test.
examples.cn: 考试时保持冷静。

examples.en: They decided to stay one more night.
examples.cn: 他们决定再住一晚。

dict_mnemonic.text: stay 是「停留」，也指「保持」和「暂住」；stay at home 是待在家里，stay in touch 是保持联系，stay calm 是保持冷静。

root: 经古法语 ester（停留）来自拉丁语 stare（站立）；站住不走，引申为停留、保持状态，以及作为客人短住。

sensesIntro.en: Stay means to remain in a place, to continue in a state, or to live somewhere briefly.
sensesIntro.cn: stay 指留在某处、保持某种状态，或短期住在某地。

core.en: Not leaving the place you are in.

branches.en: A visitor keeps to one room.
branches.cn: 来客待在一个房间里。

branches.en: A hand remains steady.
branches.cn: 一只手保持稳定。

branches.en: A guest books one more night.
branches.cn: 客人再订一晚。

branches.en: Remaining in a place and staying as a guest share one word.
branches.cn: 留在某处与做客暂住，共用同一个词。

branches.en: A state that lasts is like a guest who stays.
branches.cn: 持续的状态，就像久留的客人。

intro.en: Stay forms verb parts and nouns of remaining and visiting.
intro.cn: stay 构成动词变化，以及表示停留与做客的名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root stare also gives status, station, and static.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 stare 还衍生出 status、station 和 static。

items.example: He is a stayer in the race.
items.exampleCN: 他是比赛里能坚持到底的人。
他是全职在家带孩子的家长。

latinEntries.example: Stare is the root of stay.
latinEntries.exampleCN: stare 是 stay 的词根。

definition_en: in a firm and even way, or in a way that continues without stopping
core_image: 匀速行走的秒针
scene: 雨稳稳地下了一整夜。The rain fell steadily all night.
sceneCN: 这里 steadily 是「稳定地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：雨稳稳地下了一整夜。

senses.title: In a firm way
senses.definition: in a firm, even, and controlled way
senses.definitionCN: 以稳固、均匀而有控制的方式
senses.example: The rain fell steadily all night.
senses.exampleCN: 雨稳稳地下了一整夜。
senses.why: The basic sense is firmness without shaking.
senses.whyCN: 基本义是稳固而不摇晃。

senses.title: Without stopping
senses.definition: in a way that continues over time without stopping
senses.definitionCN: 随时间不停继续的方式
senses.example: Prices have risen steadily for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 物价持续上涨了一年。
senses.why: Something firm can also keep going.
senses.whyCN: 稳固的东西，也能一直持续下去。

senses.title: Step by step
senses.definition: in a gradual and sure way
senses.definitionCN: 以渐进且有把握的方式
senses.example: She is steadily improving her English.
senses.exampleCN: 她的英语在稳步提高。
senses.why: Steady movement is movement that does not slip back.
senses.whyCN: 稳步前进，就是不倒退的前进。

intro.en: Steadily is steady plus -ly; steady comes from stead, a place.
intro.cn: steadily 由 steady 加 -ly 构成；steady 来自 stead（位置）。

items.en: Stede meant a place or position.
Stedi meant firm in place.
Steady meant firm and even.
Steadily added the adverb ending -ly.
It described continued, gradual change.
items.cn: 它用来描述持续而渐进的变化。

note.en: Steadily is compared with look-alike words and adverbs of steady movement.
note.cn: 把 steadily 与形近词以及表示平稳移动的副词作比较。

entries.definition: in a strong and steady way

normalIntro.en: Steadily means without shaking, without stopping, and without slipping back.
normalIntro.cn: steadily 意为不摇晃、不停下，也不倒退。

normal.en: The rain fell steadily all night.
Prices have risen steadily for a year.
She is steadily improving her English.
The situation grew steadily worse.
He held the ladder steadily.

abstract.en: What is steady keeps its place while time moves.
abstract.cn: 稳固的东西，在时间流动中守住位置。

abstract.en: Small steps, repeated, become a long road.
abstract.cn: 重复的小步，走成一条长路。

abstract.en: The even beat is what makes the music hold.
abstract.cn: 均匀的节拍，让音乐站得住。

examples.en: The rain fell steadily all night.
examples.cn: 雨稳稳地下了一整夜。

examples.en: Prices have risen steadily for a year.
examples.cn: 物价持续上涨了一年。

examples.en: She is steadily improving her English.
examples.cn: 她的英语在稳步提高。

dict_mnemonic.text: steadily 由 steady 加 -ly 构成，意为「稳定地、持续地、稳步地」；rise steadily 是稳步上升，steadily improve 是稳步改善。

root: 由 steady（稳固的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成；steady 源自 stead（位置），守住位置不摇晃，便引申为稳定、持续、稳步。

sensesIntro.en: Steadily means in a firm way, without stopping, or step by step.
sensesIntro.cn: steadily 指稳定地、持续地，或一步一步稳步地。

core.en: Holding a firm line as time passes.
core.cn: 随时间推移而守住一条稳线。

branches.en: A hand holds a cup without shaking.
branches.cn: 一只手稳稳端着杯子。

branches.en: Rain keeps falling hour after hour.
branches.cn: 雨一小时接一小时地下。

branches.en: A learner climbs one step at a time.
branches.cn: 学习者一步一级往上走。

branches.en: Firmness carried through time becomes continuity.
branches.cn: 稳固贯穿时间，就成了持续。

branches.en: Continuing without a slip is moving step by step.
branches.cn: 不倒退地持续，就是一步一步前进。

intro.en: Steadily is built from steady and the adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: steadily 由 steady 与副词后缀 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; stead is an Old English word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，stead 是古英语词。
